`libovcore` is the C++17 binding of the core, made with [cxx](https://cxx.rs): accounts, vaults, sync, share
links and `.kdbx` files, on the same Rust code as the iOS, desktop and web apps. The OpenVireo desktop app
(Qt) is built on it.

- C++17 and CMake 3.21 or later, on macOS (arm64, x86_64), Linux (x86_64, arm64) and Windows x64.
- Every call that touches the network or storage **blocks** and takes a `CancelToken`. A GUI app makes them
  on a worker thread (`QtConcurrent::run`, a thread pool), never on the GUI thread.
- You write the Host (HTTP, secure store, offline cache, clock, log sink): the classes in `<host.h>`.

The binding's source, design notes and full function list are in
[`bindings/ov-ffi-cpp`](https://github.com/openvireo/openvireo-core/blob/v1.2.2/bindings/ov-ffi-cpp/README.md).

## Install

Each core release has a prebuilt CMake package per platform, `libovcore-X.Y.Z-<platform>` with `<platform>`
one of `darwin-arm64`, `darwin-x64`, `linux-arm64`, `linux-x64` (`.tar.gz`) and `windows-x64` (`.zip`).
Let CMake fetch the one you need, checked against the release's `SHA256SUMS`:

```cmake
include(FetchContent)
FetchContent_Declare(openvireo_core
    URL https://github.com/openvireo/openvireo-core/releases/download/v1.2.2/libovcore-1.2.2-linux-x64.tar.gz
    URL_HASH SHA256=<its line in SHA256SUMS>
    DOWNLOAD_EXTRACT_TIMESTAMP TRUE)
FetchContent_MakeAvailable(openvireo_core)

set(OpenVireoCore_DIR ${openvireo_core_SOURCE_DIR}/lib/cmake/OpenVireoCore)
find_package(OpenVireoCore REQUIRED)
target_link_libraries(app PRIVATE OpenVireoCore::ovcore)
```

The imported target brings the include directory, C++17 and the system libraries the static library needs.
[`cmake/OpenVireoCore.cmake`](https://github.com/openvireo/openvireo-examples-cpp/blob/main/cmake/OpenVireoCore.cmake)
in the examples picks the platform and its checksum for you; copy it.

`SHA256SUMS` is signed by the [OpenVireo release key](https://openvireo.com/verifying-signatures)
(`SHA256SUMS.asc`). To download and check a package by hand:

```sh
curl -LO https://github.com/openvireo/openvireo-core/releases/download/v1.2.2/libovcore-1.2.2-linux-x64.tar.gz
curl -LO https://github.com/openvireo/openvireo-core/releases/download/v1.2.2/SHA256SUMS
curl -LO https://github.com/openvireo/openvireo-core/releases/download/v1.2.2/SHA256SUMS.asc
gpg --verify SHA256SUMS.asc SHA256SUMS
sha256sum --ignore-missing -c SHA256SUMS
tar -xzf libovcore-1.2.2-linux-x64.tar.gz
cmake -S . -B build -DOpenVireoCore_DIR=$PWD/libovcore-1.2.2-linux-x64/lib/cmake/OpenVireoCore
```

Two other ways, for other targets or a pinned commit:

- **Build the package:** `cargo xtask cpp [--target <triple>]` in this repository writes it to
  `target/ovcore-cpp/<target>/`. On macOS it builds a universal (arm64 + x86_64) library.
- **From source with [Corrosion](https://corrosion-rs.github.io/corrosion/),** as the desktop does, so CMake
  runs cargo at a pinned commit: see
  [`bindings/ov-ffi-cpp/example`](https://github.com/openvireo/openvireo-core/blob/v1.2.2/bindings/ov-ffi-cpp/example/CMakeLists.txt). On aarch64 pass
  `--cfg aes_armv8` in the target's `RUSTFLAGS`, as the example does, or AES-KDF runs in software.

Check the install:

```cpp
#include <ovcore.h>
#include <cstdio>

int main() {
    std::printf("%s\n", std::string(ov::version()).c_str());   // 1.2.2
}
```

## A client

`ov::new_client` takes a `ClientConfig` (this device) and the five Host parts, each a class from `<host.h>`
that you implement: `HttpTransport`, `SecureStore`, `BlobCache`, `Clock` and `LogSink`. They must be
thread-safe. [`host.cpp`](https://github.com/openvireo/openvireo-examples-cpp/blob/main/src/host.cpp) in the
examples is a small Host for a command-line program: libcurl with no redirects and no cookies, memory for the
store and the cache. A desktop app keeps the store in the OS keychain and the cache on disk, so vaults open
offline.

```cpp
#include <ovcore.h>

auto cancel = ov::new_cancel_token();
ov::ClientConfig config{"", "My tool", ov::Platform::Cli, false, false, ov::ServerConfig{}};
auto client = ov::call([&] {
    return ov::new_client(config, std::make_unique<MyHttp>(), std::make_unique<MyStore>(),
                          std::make_unique<MyCache>(), std::make_unique<MyClock>(), std::make_unique<MyLog>());
});
```

## Sign in and read a field

```cpp
auto account = ov::call([&] { return client->connect("https://accounts.openvireo.com", *cancel); });
// A LoginStep that needs a TOTP code when two-step sign-in is on
ov::LoginInput input{email, std::move(password), true, std::move(secret_key), "", true};
ov::call([&] { return account->login(std::move(input), *cancel); });

auto vaults = ov::call([&] { return account->vaults(*cancel); });
auto vault = ov::call([&] { return account->open_vault(vaults[0].id, *cancel); });
auto value = ov::call([&] { return vault->read_field("ov://Personal/GitHub/username"); });
std::printf("%.*s\n", static_cast<int>(value.size()), reinterpret_cast<const char *>(value.data()));
ov::wipe(value);
ov::call([&] { account->sign_out(false, *cancel); });
```

`secret_key` is only needed the first time on a device: after a trusted sign-in the core keeps it in the
Host's secure store. Secrets go in and come out as `rust::Vec<uint8_t>`: the core wipes what you pass in, and
you wipe what comes back with `ov::wipe()`.

## Errors and cancelling

A failed call throws `rust::Error` with the text `"<wire code>: <message>"`. Wrap calls in `ov::call` to get
an `ov::Error` with the whole error instead: `code()` (the wire code, such as `"unauthorized"` or
`"plan_limit"`, the same as the TypeScript SDK's `err.code`) and `info()` with the HTTP status, retry-after
and details JSON.

```cpp
try {
    auto vaults = ov::call([&] { return account->vaults(*cancel); });
} catch (const ov::Error &e) {
    if (e.code() == "plan_limit") { /* e.info().details is JSON */ }
}
```

To cancel, keep `cancel->clone()` on another thread and call `cancel()` on it: the calls that took the token
return `aborted`.
